cim: Tech giants target spending on Florida’s state-level elections
cim_eredeti: Tech giants target spending on Florida’s state-level elections
szoveg_eredeti:
Florida’s Legislature is likely to take up artificial intelligence and data center policy in the 2027 lawmaking session.

TALLAHASSEE, Florida — Florida policymakers have aggressively pushed to regulate Big Tech companies.

Now, major corporations like Google, Meta, Amazon and Anthropic are spending in key state legislative races to fight for a seat at the table.

Tech firms are donating to Democrats and Republican candidates alike, buying scores of mailers and ads on top of making campaign contributions in the upcoming November midterms races. They’re also funneling tens of thousands of dollars — a meager sum compared to statewide races, but notable at the statehouse level — through a dizzying network of political committees that support Republican leaders in the state Legislature and lawmakers who had a hand in artificial intelligence legislation last session.

The moves could help give companies influence with state lawmakers amid a campaign cycle shaped by how Florida will respond to rapidly changing technology, with regulations likely on the agenda again in 2027. The contributions, some of which have not been previously reported, also provide a deeper look at where Big Tech’s priorities lie ahead of the first major election since AI and data center issues took center stage in Tallahassee.
